- Shows the fallback/exception process if SLAs aren't met, including credits calculation and reporting cadence.

Hi Amal — thanks, and glad the demo landed well. We're able to put together a draft SLO/SLA addendum and proposed order-form text for the Dedicated capacity line items. High level: 

- Uptime: we can offer a contractual uptime target of 99.95% monthly for the Dedicated pool referenced in the SOW, with standard exclusions (scheduled maintenance windows with 48h notice, agreed blackout windows for migrations, and force majeure).
- Latency: for latency we recommend a p95 SLO (e.g., 1200ms for 1k-token responses) and call it an "SLO-backed latency objective" rather than a hard SLA. Latency is highly dependent on model selection, sequence length, and batching; we can make latency commitments for defined request profiles in Appendix A.
- Credits & reporting: propose a credit table (monthly credits up to X% of monthly fee capped at 50%) plus a monthly SLA report and a 30-day remediation plan trigger for consecutive misses.

I'm attaching a first-pass addendum (Redwood_SLO_Addendum_draft_v1.pdf) and a short snippet you can drop into the order form that references the addendum and appendix. Laura and Marcus are looped in to confirm legal/finance redlines.

If this direction works, I'll incorporate any redlines and circulate a DocuSign envelope for the order form + addendum.

Thanks,

Brief legal redlines and suggested order-form language below (excerpt):

--- Proposed order form clause (for insertion into Order Form / SOW):
"Service Availability: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain Service Availability of 99.95% measured per calendar month for the Dedicated deployment(s) identified in the Order Form. Service Availability will be calculated as: (Total minutes in month - Minutes of Unavailable Service) / Total minutes in month. Unavailable Service excludes Scheduled Maintenance (see below), Customer-caused failures, and Force Majeure."

"Latency Objective: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to meet the following latency objective for inference requests to the dedicated endpoint: p95 <= 1200ms for request profiles defined in Appendix A. Latency Objective is an operational target and is not a monetary SLA. Repeated misses to the Latency Objective will trigger the operational remediation process but will not automatically result in service credits unless otherwise agreed in writing."

"Service Credits: For Service Availability below the target in any calendar month, Customer will be eligible for a service credit equal to 5% of the monthly dedicated fee for each 0.1% below the target, up to a maximum of 50% of the monthly dedicated fee for that month. To receive a credit, Customer must submit a credit request within 30 days of the month-end and provide any requested logs and cooperation for root cause analysis."

Notes: add a clause for "SLO Exception Process" — route for requesting temporary exceptions (e.g., planned maintenance >8h, load tests) that require approval from VP of Product & VP Sales (or their designees). Also recommend explicit reporting cadence (monthly SLA dashboard plus ad-hoc incident reports within 72h).

Marcus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
